channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: I built an unofficial Azur Promilia wiki with launch-day tools — here's the data model
item.description: A game launched worldwide today and its player-made wiki went live the same morning — here is how the site's launch-day tools and data model were built.

item.title: Building Clockwork: An AI-Native 2D Game Engine Verified End-to-End with Kane CLI
item.description: Clockwork packs scene building, behaviors, rules, HUD design and playtesting into one browser app, with Kane CLI driving real Chrome to prove the editor and its games work end to end.

item.title: Godot 4: Image size must match texture's image size.
item.description: When uploading layers into an ImageTextureLayered, any mismatch in size or format silently rejects the upload; this troubleshooting note explains why the error appears and how to track it down.

item.title: A pre-export checklist for Blender textures (before Unity or Godot)
item.description: Missing textures in Unity or Godot are usually export mistakes, not engine bugs — this pre-export checklist catches them in Blender before they cost you a rework.

item.title: Data-Driven Units for a Turn-Based Strategy Game: A Schema Checklist Before Your Team Splits the Content Work
item.description: Turn-based strategy games multiply a few systems across dozens of units — this schema checklist helps teams lock down unit data before splitting the content work.

item.title: My AI game master lied about who was in the room. That bug became an agent-honesty checker.
item.description: An AI game master claimed a character standing next to the player wasn't there — and described a living companion as a corpse. That bug became an agent-honesty checker.

item.title: A pre-export checklist for Blender textures (before Unity or Godot)
item.description: Missing textures in Unity or Godot are usually export mistakes, not engine bugs — this pre-export checklist catches them in Blender before they cost you a rework.

item.title: A checked vehicle is not a verified fact: separate progress from evidence
item.description: The author of LeonidaRides, an indie game vehicle reference tool, explains a design rule: a player checking an item off is not the same as an editor verifying a fact, so progress and evidence stay separate.

item.title: Hydrilla AI tutorial: how much does one 3D asset actually cost? The $0.12 per prop math
item.description: This independent tutorial works through Hydrilla AI's official pricing page, FAQ, and Terms of Service to break down the roughly $0.12 cost of a single 3D prop, helping developers judge whether AI-generated assets are actually worth it.

item.title: Choosing a Game Engine Before You Hire: A Decision Sheet for Founders Building a Team in India
item.description: A decision sheet for founders hiring a team in India: pick target devices before picking an engine, and weigh hiring, cost and platform trade-offs up front.

item.title: How a Rust civ sim stays deterministic with WebAssembly SIMD and threads
item.description: A browser civilization sim written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly; the author breaks down the fixed tick order and spatial indexing that keep the world evolving identically with SIMD or threads enabled.

item.title: Ensō Engine 1.1: a free Blender build for anime and NPR
item.description: Mix 3D Design released Ensō Engine 1.1, a free open-source Blender build tailored for anime and non-photorealistic rendering.

item.title: Localizing a Game for Turkish: the Dotted I, Suffixes on Placeholders and Other Engine Problems
item.description: Turkish looks like an easy Latin-alphabet locale until misspelled menus, broken item messages, and crashes only Turkish players can reproduce show up — the article unpacks each engineering pitfall.

item.title: How I Built a Daily Chart-Guessing Game on Reddit (And Why the Crowd Keeps Winning)
item.description: The author looks back at a daily chart-guessing game built on Reddit — scoring zero on day two — and unpacks the design pitfalls of data-visualization games and the wisdom of the crowd.

item.title: Ludo.ai launches AI-powered Tileset Generator for 2D game development
item.description: Describe a tileset in words and get a full set of 2D map tiles, a handy new tool for pixel-art and top-down level work.

item.title: Running a Two-Week Character Style Test Before You Commit to Stylised or Realistic
item.description: Many small teams settle their character style in a single meeting; the author suggests a structured two-week style test before committing, so the choice doesn't lock in hiring, tools and the publisher pitch too early.

item.title: Roblox signs music licensing agreement with PRS for Music
item.description: Roblox signs a music licensing deal with UK rights body PRS for Music, opening a new revenue stream for songwriters and publishers whose music is used on the platform, with royalty payments starting in 2027.

item.title: 5 things I learned building a 3D map editor in Rust with Bevy
item.description: The author spent months building Fiza3D, a desktop 3D map editor for game levels, roads, and cities in Rust on Bevy, and shares five lessons for anyone wanting to build a similar tool.

item.title: Ziva VFX-Inspired Physics-Based Muscle Simulation Tool For 3ds Max, Maya, Blender & Houdini
item.description: HézFX brings muscle, fascia, fat, and skin into one unified simulation, giving animated characters a more believable sense of flesh in motion.

item.title: How Hyperscales was built, part 1: We woke it up - the audit and what we found
item.description: The first devlog in a series on rescuing a half-forgotten prototype into a presentable game in two days, starting with what the code audit uncovered.
